jordan_cust: Hey support — running into a weird rerank problem. We embed docs with `text-embedding-1024-v1` (1024 dims) and then call /rerank using `rerank-bert-768`. No error from the API, but top scores look wildly inflated and the ranking is totally wrong. Example: the top doc is unrelated but score=0.98, other highly related docs get ~0.4.

jordan_cust: Request info: Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d, timestamps around 2026-02-20T14:12Z.

alice_support: Thanks — can you paste the exact payload you're sending to /rerank and the length of the vector you pass? Also did you generate embeddings client-side or via our /embeddings endpoint?

jordan_cust: We call our embedding service (server-side) which proxies to your hosted embeddings. Simplified payloads below: 

```json
// embedding call (we store output)
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "text-embedding-1024-v1", "input": "Some document text..." }
// response contains: {"embedding": [0.0012, -0.345, ...] } // len = 1024

// rerank call
POST /v1/rerank
{ "model": "rerank-bert-768", "query_vector": [0.0009, -0.310, ...], "candidates": [{"id":"d1","vector":[...len=1024...]}, ...] }
```

jordan_cust: We verified the stored vector length: 1024 for several docs. We assumed rerank would accept different dims (and internally hash/normalize), but it's producing nonsense.

pat_oncall: @alice_support / @jordan_cust — this rings like an embedding-dimension incompatibility. Reranker models are built with a fixed expected dim (here 768). Historically, the runtime had a len check that allowed vectors <= max_dim and then silently truncated or padded to fit the internal representation. That produced subtle dot-product scaling issues because truncation removed high-signal components. So it didn't throw a hard error — it just produced bad scores.

pat_oncall: Quick debug: did you fetch any server logs with `rerank.shape_check` entries? If not, I can pull the trace for r-0a1b2c3d.

jordan_cust: I don't have direct server logs. Here's the raw response we get from rerank: 

```json
{ "results": [ {"id":"d7","score":0.982, "metadata":{...} }, {"id":"d3","score":0.412 } ] }
```

jordan_cust: Scores > 1 occasionally showed up too (we saw 1.03 once) — which made us think normalization or mismatched dims were at play.

mia_ml: Confirming @pat_oncall's suspicion. The runtime bug: shape validation used `<= model.max_dim` check instead of strict equality with model.expected_dim. For some incompatible model pairs (embed larger than rerank), we were slicing the vector to the first N dims without any log line visible to customers. That combined with no L2 normalization applied consistently leads to unpredictable dot-product magnitudes.

mia_ml: Immediate mitigation options: 
- Recompute embeddings with a 768-dim model (recommended)
- If that's not possible, L2-normalize your 1024-d vectors and then downsample deterministically (e.g., take first 768 dims) — this helps but is lossy.
- As a temporary server-side workaround we can enable strict mode for your account which will reject mismatched dims with 400 and a clear message.

alice_support: To be explicit for your engineers: please switch to an embedding model that matches the rerank model family (or the same dim). If you want us to enable strict-mode on your org id so you get explicit 400s, we'll do that ASAP while we push the runtime fix. Would you like us to enable it? :point_down:

jordan_cust: Yes please enable strict-mode for our org. We prefer failing fast so we can fix the pipeline. Also can you confirm whether there are any billing implications if we re-embed a subset?

alice_support: Enabling strict-mode won't change billing. Re-embedding is charged as normal embeddings usage. If you want, we can scope a re-embed job for only top-k docs first to reduce cost. I can introduce you to solutions-eng for help.

pat_oncall: I pulled the trace for r-0a1b2c3d — confirmed the slice happened at the C++ kernel boundary. File a ticket in infra with label `rerank-dim` and I'll attach the trace. Root cause: permissive shape check + truncation. Fix planned: strict equality check + telemetry + clear error message. Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4521 (canary already).

mia_ml: Hotfix details:
```
// pseudocode
expected = model.expected_dim
if len(vec) != expected:
  raise BadRequest("embedding dimension mismatch: expected %d got %d" % (expected, len(vec)))
// also add metric: rerank.mismatch_count++
```
Canary -> prod rollout scheduled in 30 min.

deploy-bot: Hotfix deployment: runtime/rerank shape-check v1.0.2 rolled to canary at 2026-02-20T14:45Z. Watch: #eng-runtime.

alice_support: OK I enabled strict-mode on your org (org-555). Going forward you'll see 400s with a clear message if dims mismatch. Workaround steps I recommend now: 
1) Re-embed query + docs with a 768-d model OR
2) If you must keep 1024 embeddings, call our /embeddings with `model: "text-embedding-768-v1"` for rerank paths only.

jordan_cust: Thanks everyone — we re-embedded ~2k documents with 768 and re-ran the rerank test. Ranking looks correct now (top hit is relevant, scores in expected 0.6-0.9 range). Will monitor production and open a follow-up if we see regressions. :tada:

alice_support: Great — closing loop here. We'll post a short incident note and update the docs to call out cross-model incompatibility for embed+rerank mixes. If you want a postmortem or help with a scoped re-embed job, ping me or @solutions-eng. :thumbsup:
